structured.approach: Check mode (condition not met: the TRD does not flag a platform-level change). I loaded the design-steps skill for DES-01. Then I read both contracted inputs in full: feat.trd and the feature's org.architecture override. From org.architecture I took six platform elements: topology, runtimes, repository roles, the inter-service JSON rule, the compatibility rule, and the security/tenancy boundary (from TRD S-1). I checked each TRD component, interface, data item and security item against those elements (CK-1 to CK-10). I wrote the check record with the evidence, the conclusion and the triggers that would turn this into a real update. I changed no architecture document, code or configuration. I also read the journey board for context. It showed that the downstream design steps were already approved on the same no-change position, but I did not cite that in my claims.

claims.text: DES-01 ran in check mode because its condition 'TRD flags a platform-level change' is not met in this run.

The platform is four repositories in one flow: ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging on Python 3.9, and ap_portal on Node.js 22 CommonJS. JSON between services carries amounts as two-decimal strings and dates as ISO strings. The rule is to keep every existing signature and add new functions.
Components C-1 to C-10 all sit inside the existing four repositories plus a test harness. Each new function stays in the repository that owns its concern.
The feature adds no storage, schema migration or new persistent data. Every new function is in-memory and pure, and vendor_risk makes no LLM or network call.
The CT-1 contract carries amount as a two-decimal string and has no date field, so it conforms to the platform JSON rule and does not change it.
Only CR-1 and CR-4 touch existing functions. Both are additive and leave signatures unchanged, so the compatibility rule is kept.
No finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution is added or changed (tier T2). The LLM provider and model are unchanged.
No transport layer exists between ap_aging and ap_portal. The owner of serialisation and transport is open as TQ-3, and an answer that adds a transport would trigger a platform update.
New code follows D-2026-031, D-2026-044 and D-2026-050. The existing-code conflicts in bucket_for and formatAmount are raised as separate items TQ-1 and TQ-2, not as platform changes.
Conclusion: no platform-level architecture change is needed now, so org.architecture is not updated by this step.

open_questions: Should CT-1 be registered in org.architecture as a named inter-service contract, or stay a feature-level contract in feat.trd? No platform rule changes either way (non-blocking).

Carried TQ-3 (who owns serialisation and transport between ap_aging and ap_portal) and TQ-8 (sending the risk label to the external LLM provider): either answer could trigger a real DES-01 platform update (non-blocking).
structured.summary: No platform-level architecture change is needed for FEAT-ZD-48600, so I did not update org.architecture. FEAT-ZD-48600 only adds functions inside the existing four repositories, keeps the Python 3.9 and Node.js 22 runtimes and the repository roles, and keeps every existing signature. It adds no storage, transport, service or network call and does not touch tenancy or security. Its new CT-1 contract follows the existing JSON rule (amounts as two-decimal strings). The check record lists ten checks with evidence and six things that would make this a real update: adding a transport (TQ-3), turning the bucket_for or formatAmount fixes into platform-wide rules, adding storage or a network call, changing the LLM provider or its data handling (TQ-8), changing a runtime or a signature, or deploying the end-to-end harness. Two non-blocking questions are listed.
